::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

This section is adapted from @zhou2024eig,
used under the MIT License
(see the license text in @sec-subspaces).
These notes take eigenvalues to be real numbers (@def-eigenvalue),
so the source's complex eigenvalues are left out,
and eigenvalues are characterized through null spaces
rather than through the characteristic polynomial.
Only the source's material on similarity, diagonalization and the basic eigenvalue properties is adapted;
its characteristic polynomial and algebraic multiplicity,
its trace and determinant identities,
and the part of its section on symmetric matrices that builds bases of the column space and null space from eigenvectors are left out.
The rest of that section is covered by @thm-spectral and @thm-symmetric-eigenvectors-orthogonal.
Its result that eigenvalues of orthogonal matrices have modulus $1$ appears here in the real form $\pm 1$.
Three other parts of the source are not part of this section:

- its statement that the eigenvalues of a lower triangular matrix are also its diagonal entries (@thm-eigen-triangular states the upper triangular case)
- its three further examples of matrices with geometric multiplicity smaller than algebraic multiplicity
  (@exm-eigenspace gives one nilpotent example)
- its code cells
The source's two-vector argument that eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are independent
is extended here to any number of eigenvectors.

:::
